original_question: Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P, determine which Hamiltonian cycle of G corresponds to the boundary of P.
target_in_paper: §4.4, Open Problem 34 (Hamiltonian Cycle in Visibility Graphs).
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s exact target: it correctly identifies that the input is a visibility graph G coming from a simple polygon and that the goal is to recover the Hamiltonian cycle representing the polygon boundary. This is exactly the subject of §4.4, Open Problem 34.
missing_details: The paper means the vertex visibility graph of an unknown simple polygon P; P itself is not given as geometric input.
The graph is promised to be the visibility graph of some simple polygon; this is not the broader recognition problem of deciding whether an arbitrary graph is such a visibility graph.

In this paper’s polygon setting, two polygon vertices are adjacent in G exactly when the straight segment joining them lies entirely within P; the definition allows the segment to pass through a reflex vertex or graze along a polygon edge.
The intended task is to identify the boundary Hamiltonian cycle among potentially several Hamiltonian cycles in G.
Section 4 concerns simple polygons; the statement should not be broadened to polygons with holes.
The paper does not attach a complexity requirement such as polynomial time to Open Problem 34, so adding one would change the scope.
No ambient ring/field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or 'sufficiently large' quantifiers are relevant here; this is a graph-theoretic visibility problem.
refined_question: Let G be given, with the promise that G is the vertex visibility graph of some simple polygon P. Here the vertices of G correspond to the vertices of P, and two vertices are adjacent exactly when the line segment joining the corresponding polygon vertices lies entirely inside P (as defined in the paper, allowing the segment to pass through a reflex vertex or graze along a polygon edge). Since G may contain several Hamiltonian cycles, determine which Hamiltonian cycle of G is the one induced by the cyclic order of the vertices on the boundary of P.
justification: The draft matches Open Problem 34 almost verbatim. The nearby context in §1 supplies the exact polygon-visibility definition, while §4.1 explains that recognition becomes easier when the boundary Hamiltonian cycle is already given, which confirms that Open Problem 34 is specifically about recovering that cycle from G alone rather than solving a broader recognition or reconstruction problem. Sections 4.6 and 4.7 reinforce this reading by treating the boundary Hamiltonian cycle as additional input for later algorithmic questions. Because Open Problem 34 itself does not impose a complexity bound, the refined question should stay neutral on algorithmic complexity.
